title: Make Vulnerability A CX Priority
summary: Discover how leading organizations move beyond compliance and proactively identify, support, and protect vulnerable customers to build trust.
body_markdown:
Too many organizations still reduce customer vulnerability to a compliance exercise. That’s a mistake. When firms focus primarily on policies, disclosures, and remediation after harm occurs, they miss an opportunity to better support customers and build trust.


Customers experiencing vulnerability or additional needs exist across every customer population, yet many organizations only provide support after customers encounter significant difficulties. Our new report,[How To Better Identify, Support, And Protect Vulnerable Customers](https://www.forrester.com/report/how-to-better-identify-support-and-protect-vulnerable-customers/RES201701?ref_search=2881951_1789404978628) , argues that firms must move from reactive support to proactive protection by identifying emerging needs earlier and reducing barriers before harm occurs.


#### **Identify Vulnerability Before Customers Ask For Help**


Vulnerability touches more customers than many firms realise and is not limited to a specific customer segment. Financial pressures, illness, disability, bereavement, fraud, major life events, and changing levels of digital confidence can all affect customers, often unexpectedly. Because circumstances change over time, organizations cannot rely on static segmentation or wait for customers to self-identify.


#### Remove Experience Barriers That Increase Vulnerability


Customer circumstances can influence vulnerability. But organizations also create and amplify vulnerability through the experiences they design. Complex communications, inaccessible digital experiences, fragmented journeys, and inflexible processes can make it harder for customers to access services, understand options, and make informed decisions.


#### **Shift From Reactive Support To Proactive Protection**


Leading organizations increasingly view customer protection as a trust-building capability. They focus on identifying needs earlier, adapting support as circumstances change, and removing barriers before they lead to poor outcomes.


This benefits customers through better accessibility, lower effort, and timely support. It also benefits firms by reducing complaints, remediation costs, fraud losses, and conduct risks while increasing trust and loyalty.


#### **Use AI To Anticipate Needs, But Do So Responsibly**


AI can help organizations detect emerging needs, personalize support, and intervene earlier. But it can also make vulnerability less visible if models rely on incomplete or biased data. As firms embed AI across customer journeys, they must ensure that automation supports fair treatment and good outcomes, particularly for vulnerable customers.


Regulators are increasingly focused on these risks. For instance, in line with the[FCA’s Consumer Duty](https://www.fca.org.uk/firms/consumer-duty) , UK financial services providers must be able to demonstrate that AI-enabled processes support fair treatment and good customer outcomes.


#### **Strengthen Trust Through Better Outcomes**


Organizations that identify needs earlier, design more inclusive experiences, and coordinate support across channels can improve both customer and business outcomes. Rather than treating vulnerability as a downstream support process, they embed it into the design of products, services, journeys, and experiences from the outset.
